answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a state-issued ID, checked for uniqueness against a global registry. Enrollment proves one civil registry number backs one credential; the registry refuses repeats. The scarce resource is the legal person: one number per human, so a thousand clones need a thousand recruited people. Each identity is one comet with its own number, not a spiral of clones minting off one person. The one signal a clone cannot forge is a live human's record. Assumes an honest issuer; a rich attacker can hire people, so it caps cheap minting, not wealth.
